claims.text: Replacing conventional EAM references with a machine-learning interatomic potential will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in thermodynamic integration.
The machine-learning potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to conventional EAM references.
The proposed potential should be trained on ab initio configurations from both disordered solid and liquid states near melting.
High-entropy alloys are typically equiatomic or contain at least five principal elements.
The proposed method is applicable from approximately 0.8 to 1.1 times the alloy melting temperature.
The high-temperature liquid explores a wide range of atomic configurations.
A machine-learning potential can capture many-body interactions and diverse local atomic environments relevant to these alloys.
Capturing these interactions and environments will make configurations sampled by the reference more similar to ab initio configurations.
Training on a broad ab initio dataset will allow the machine-learning potential to reproduce the complex energy landscapes of both solid and liquid states.
Reproducing the solid and liquid energy landscapes will enhance phase-space overlap.
Enhanced phase-space overlap will reduce mismatch along the thermodynamic-integration path relative to EAM-based TOR-TILD.
The intervention will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 30–50% relative to the EAM baseline.
The intervention will produce free-energy estimates that agree more closely with direct ab initio calculations than EAM-based estimates do.
Improvement is expected when the alloy's relevant high-temperature configurations are well represented in the ab initio training data.
Effectiveness may be limited by extreme compositional inhomogeneity.
Effectiveness may be limited at temperatures far outside the potential's calibrated range.
The magnitude of mismatch reduction depends on the quality and representativeness of the ab initio training set.
